Rule 54 will also fail to universally reach short cycles within 4*W steps.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the worst-case transient + cycle length for Rule 184 on W in 5..11 exceeds 4*W, the conservation bounding argument fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the order of the Rule 90 adjacency matrix modulo 2 for all W in 5..11 has a maximum period of 1 or 2, then Rule 90 would unexpectedly satisfy the bound.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Rule 110 does not exhibit a cycle longer than 2 or transient extending beyond 4*W for W <= 11, its universality does not manifest within these finite bounds.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Rule 184 is a number-conserving, right-shift-permissive CA that acts as a traffic model. Its local transition function strictly conserves the total number of live (1) cells in the lattice. On a ring of width W, the state space is partitioned into invariant classes of size C(W, k) where k is the number of 1s. The dynamics within each class are governed by a deterministic permutation equivalent to sorting adjacent particles, bounding the maximum possible transient and cycle length by W (specifically, the worst-case bottleneck is W steps for a block of half-density traffic). Thus, the global maximum transient + cycle length is less than 2W, easily satisfying the 4W step bound. In contrast, Rule 90 is a linear cellular automaton over GF(2). Its temporal evolution is computed by raising the adjacency matrix of the cycle graph C_W to the power t. The order of this matrix modulo 2 determines the cycle length. For W = 6, the characteristic polynomial includes factors that yield an order of 6, meaning an initial state exists with a pure period-6 cycle. Since 6 > 2, it violates the 'cycle length at most 2' bound (and starting from a shifted state yields a transient). Rule 110 is computationally universal, implying arbitrarily long transients for sufficiently large W. By structural analogy, Rule 54 is also known to support complex interacting gliders and particle-like dynamics, meaning it lacks the conservation/ballistic sorting property of 184. We predict Rule 54 will also fail the bound for some W in 5..11 due to glider interactions producing cycles longer than 2.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
